systems.name: Physical Mechanics System
systems.summary: Governs the physical setup and hand technique required before any musical content is addressed. Establishes equipment standards, picking flexibility, left-right synchronization, and hand economy as the non-negotiable foundation for all subsequent development.

members.name: Equipment Setup
members.summary: String gauge (.012 minimum), medium-high action, and medium-to-heavy celluloid picks are prescribed to build resistance and develop both hands. Metronome, tape recorder, and timer are mandatory practice tools.

members.name: Right-Hand Technique
members.summary: Flexibility is the governing principle; rigid anchor systems (elbow, wrist, pick-guard) create speed ceilings under tension. Alternate picking with dynamic equality between up and down strokes is the required method.

members.name: Left-Hand Technique
members.summary: Perpendicular finger angle (hammer-like), thumb centered on neck back, minimal finger lift, and flat wrist posture together constitute correct left-hand form.

members.name: Left-Right Hand Synchronization
members.summary: Perfect simultaneous attack by both hands is non-negotiable. Any flam (finger-first or pick-first) produces two sounds.

traversal_rules.name: Accuracy Precedes Speed
traversal_rules.summary: Speed is a byproduct of accuracy and is unattainable without it. Tempo goals must never be pursued at the expense of precision.

references.quote_excerpt: Care should be taken not to sacrifice accuracy and precision in order to meet the tempo goals

traversal_rules.name: Flexibility Over Fixed Anchor
traversal_rules.summary: Right-hand technique must remain adaptable. Any fixed anchor system becomes a hard speed ceiling when tempos increase.

references.quote_excerpt: flexibility-the ability to adapt the right hand to a variety of moves-is the key to longevity
avoid is any kind of anchor system that inhibits freedom of movement

traversal_rules.name: No-Flam Synchronization Law
traversal_rules.summary: Left and right hands must attack each note simultaneously. Flams in either direction produce two audible sounds. Diagnosis requires very slow play across the full fingerboard.

references.quote_excerpt: the left and right hands must be in perfect synchronization. No Flams!
play tones very slowly at all points on the fingerboard

traversal_rules.name: Alternate Picking Stroke Equality
traversal_rules.summary: Only alternate picking is permitted during project lessons. Upstrokes must sound as strong as downstrokes.

references.quote_excerpt: strive to make up strokes sound as strong as down strokes

traversal_rules.name: Correct-Hand Blame Attribution
traversal_rules.summary: Before attempting any technical fix, correctly identify which hand is at fault.

references.quote_excerpt: A most common mistake is to blame the left hand when the right hand is at fault

modification_rules.name: Legato Techniques Unlocked at Week 15
modification_rules.summary: Hammer-ons, pull-offs, and glissandi are forbidden during Weeks 1-13. They are introduced in Weeks 15-17 specifically because they produce multiple notes per pick stroke.

references.quote_excerpt: via these devices several notes can be produced with one picking stroke
No hammer-on's. No pull-offts. No other ornamentation

systems.name: Fingerboard Harmony System
systems.summary: Organizes the entire guitar neck through key-center analysis and five movable scale patterns. Chord progressions are understood as belonging to key centers rather than treated chord-by-chord; arpeggios, scales, and interval skips are deployed within that framework to build harmonically grounded improvised lines.

members.name: Key Center Analysis
members.summary: Diatonic harmony is generated by stacking a major or minor scale in thirds. Chord progressions are assigned to a single key center identified analytically and ultimately by ear.

members.name: Five Movable Scale Patterns
members.summary: Five finger-per-fret patterns cover the full fingerboard for any key. Tonics are circled for visual targeting. Patterns are connected by three moves: position skips, stretching, and sliding on half steps.

members.name: Melodic Toolkit
members.summary: Six scale types, arpeggios, interval skips (diatonically derived), and common tones constitute the complete melodic arsenal.

traversal_rules.name: Key-Center-First Navigation
traversal_rules.summary: When moving to a new key center in a progression, select one of the five scale patterns for that key and improvise within that region.

references.quote_excerpt: for each new one, move your hand to a convenient fingering pattern for that particular scale
arpeggios will be easier to handle if they are played within a scale pattern

traversal_rules.name: Three-Move Pattern Connection
traversal_rules.summary: Moving between the five patterns is achieved by exactly three techniques: position skips, stretching to the adjacent pattern, or sliding on the half step between patterns.

references.quote_excerpt: There are essentially three moves involved in moving from one pattern to another

traversal_rules.name: Diatonic Interval Skip Derivation
traversal_rules.summary: Interval skips must be derived from the scale's half steps, producing combinations of major and minor intervals rather than parallel intervals.

references.quote_excerpt: playing scale intervals that take into account the half steps of the scale

traversal_rules.name: Consecutive Scale Tone Ceiling
traversal_rules.summary: No more than 3-4 consecutive scale tones in the same direction are permitted before changing direction or introducing a skip.

references.quote_excerpt: don't play more than 3 or 4 scale tones in the same direction

traversal_rules.name: Common Tone Relief
traversal_rules.summary: Sustained common tones are a legitimate device to flatten the melodic line and relieve excessive vertical movement.

references.quote_excerpt: A common tone is a note that is common to two or more chords

traversal_rules.name: Ear as Final Harmonic Arbiter
traversal_rules.summary: Key-center brackets represent one analysis. Chord substitution and alternative key interpretations are freely available. The ear is the final arbiter.

references.quote_excerpt: If they're right, they will sound right and if they're wrong, you will know it immediately

modification_rules.name: Harmonic Minor Derived from Diatonic Pattern
modification_rules.summary: Harmonic minor patterns are derived from already-learned diatonic patterns by raising the fifth scale step.

references.quote_excerpt: learned by simply sharping the fifth scale step of the diatonic scales

modification_rules.name: Transposition as Creative Stimulus
modification_rules.summary: Repeating a project lesson in a transposed key forces new fingering patterns and stimulates fresh melodic ideas.

references.quote_excerpt: requires a change of fingering patterns, licks, etc. This also tends to stimulate fresh approaches

systems.name: Practice Discipline System
systems.summary: Governs the structural, psychological, and scheduling requirements for executing the 20-week program. Covers daily session format, schedule adherence, the growth plateau cycle, the 21-day imprinting threshold, and the principle that technique training serves spontaneous musical invention.

members.name: Session Structure
members.summary: 50-minute daily sessions, six consecutive days per week, one day off. Three phases: duple (Weeks 1-6), triple (Weeks 8-13), tempo solidification with legato (Weeks 15-17). Target: ♩=126.

members.name: Psychological Framework
members.summary: The growth plateau cycle inverts subjective experience: struggle signals neurological growth; felt fluency signals a rest period.

members.name: Improvisation Ethos
members.summary: Technique training exists to enable spontaneous invention. Model solos are reference material, not prescriptions.

traversal_rules.name: Absolute Schedule Adherence
traversal_rules.summary: Results are attainable only through exact compliance: no missed days, no shortened sessions, no out-of-sequence introductions of techniques.

references.quote_excerpt: attainable only if the reader follows each step of the program without deviation
Avoid skipping a day, for whatever reason. The effect is hazardous to progress

traversal_rules.name: 21-Day Permanent Imprinting Threshold
traversal_rules.summary: Maintaining a given tempo for approximately 21 consecutive days permanently locks that ability into the nervous system as a motor reflex.

references.quote_excerpt: approximately 21 days, on a daily basis, the ability acquired during that period of time will be permanently imprinted

traversal_rules.name: Metronome as Progress Tracker, Not Target
traversal_rules.summary: The metronome records progress; it is never set to a desired speed as a goal.

references.quote_excerpt: Do not set your metronome to a desired speed and try to rise to meet it

traversal_rules.name: Growth Plateau Cycle Invert Subjective Signal
traversal_rules.summary: The feeling of getting nowhere is the signal of active neurological development. The feeling of great progress signals a rest plateau.

references.quote_excerpt: The progress was made during the uphill climb, not during the rest period

traversal_rules.name: Technique Serves Spontaneous Invention
traversal_rules.summary: All technical training exists to remove obstacles to the immediate realization of musical ideas.

references.quote_excerpt: The important consideration is the spontaneous invention of your own solo line

traversal_rules.name: Memorize Changes to Free Attention
traversal_rules.summary: Chord changes must be memorized and removed from the page as quickly as possible to free cognitive attention.

references.quote_excerpt: Memorizing the chord changes allows you to focus all of your attention on what you are playing

modification_rules.name: Group Practice as Phase Accelerator
modification_rules.summary: Ensemble exchange (trading solos and comping with other guitarists) is superior to solo practice for this program.

references.quote_excerpt: The group dynamics is superior to private study for a program of this sort

modification_rules.name: Line Construction Entry-Point Tools
modification_rules.summary: When improvisation stalls, three structured entry points are available: melody sketch over changes, question-and-answer form, and sing before playing.

references.quote_excerpt: A very common form for building a solo line is: QUESTION AND ANSWER
sing the solo
